instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Acknowledge Our History
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize that the relationship, memory, or sacrifice mattered and cannot be treated as incidental.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll clear this shelf, but our allotment photo stays out. That summer gets a proper place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We grew three carrots. I need the shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You'll have the shelf. I'll find another spot. Those three carrots got us watering together every morning; that's the part we're keeping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I could put the photo on my desk at work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, I'll clean the frame for you. And when someone laughs at the harvest, tell them about those mornings. You can tell it your way; I just want our summer to mean more than three carrots.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sort the holiday box. Our ferry ticket goes in the keep pile; we worked too much overtime for that weekend to disappear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We missed the ferry. I hate being reminded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the ticket needn't be on top. I'll pack it away. But we stayed together instead of going home for a refund; that choice belongs in the box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep the hotel receipt instead. That part was lovely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Receipt it is. I'll get an envelope; you write 'that part was lovely' on it, however you like. We'll keep your version. I need it in your handwriting so this isn't just my campaign to make the weekend count.

cards.title: Choose the Relationship
cards.instruction: Make someone prioritize this connection over a competing person, promise, or opportunity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've set aside this half-hour for our wedding vows. Let work ring; we'll finish our promises first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The client won't sign unless I'm there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll do ten minutes, and I'll have your coat ready. We still come before the client for those ten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask Maya to cover the call. She'll want a reason.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her we're choosing our vows. I'll type while you speak so we use the time well. Put it in the calendar as our appointment; I want her covering for something you chose, not an unexplained delay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dinner's at seven. I've learned your mother's dumplings, and tonight we're eating together instead of going to that networking dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director's coming. I could get promoted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll eat at six. I'll do the clearing up; you can wear the suit. But give this evening to us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Freeze them. We'll have them tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That was the anniversary plan too. I'll freeze the leftovers, but put two on plates now. Call and say you're having dinner with me. We can eat quickly; I need you to choose being here, not just another date for the dumplings.

cards.title: Remember Me Correctly
cards.instruction: Create small tests of whether someone remembers your preferences, stories, or shared history.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll run the tea tray. Before I pour, pick out my cup; let's see what twelve years of breakfast have taught you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone's waiting. Can't you just take one?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll carry the tray through; you only have to point. Quick decision: which one's always been mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Blue. I can see your name through the glass cupboard door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Correct. I'll take it out and keep the tray moving. One last quick choice while I pour: how much milk? That answer isn't printed on the cup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before you caption our holiday photo, what did I say when we missed that boat? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember you laughing. Not the words.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'll start you off: 'Well, that's the last time we trust...'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just write 'Happy memories'?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's try multiple choice. Your watch, my French, or the man selling us watches?

cards.title: Let Go of the Grudge
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender resentment, distance, or a claim that keeps the relationship stuck.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put our plates together. We'll have dinner side by side tonight, even though I missed your opening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left that seat empty. I'm eating at the other end tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I earned that. I'll move the food to your end instead; you needn't move. But let me sit beside you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm still going to tell you everything you missed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, we'll start there. I'll serve while you tell it, and I won't defend myself between scenes. Leave the next chair free; I'll bring both plates over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the fragile things for your move. Missing your birthday doesn't have to keep me out of every box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I needed you then. You didn't show.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're right. Pick one box, then, and tell me how you want it carried. I'll start there and stay until the job's done.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The birthday glasses. Still wrapped, because nobody came.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Glasses first, then. I'll keep them beside me in the car; you can check every one when we arrive. Could we unwrap two together? I'll do all the washing up. I don't want you still drinking alone because I missed that night.

cards.title: I Pulled Away First
cards.instruction: Hide your role in creating the distance while working urgently to repair it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before your taxi comes, let's restart our letters. I've brought paper and stamps. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You never answered my last three.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. The post's been terrible. We can write the first ones here, bypass the whole system.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I handed you the last one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better. Sit down; I'll write yours first. You can watch until there's enough to take home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've sorted lunch and your new key. Come in now; we'll get back to our usual Sunday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You changed the lock without telling me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This key does both doors. You choose which to try first; I'll carry your bag while you check. Lunch can wait a minute.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stood outside on my birthday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll put candles on lunch. I'll find them while you let yourself in; choose where we sit, anywhere you like. We'll start the afternoon properly. Just stay while I get the candles.
